content: ASME BPVC text is copyrighted; redistributing code PDFs/clauses without license is prohibited (pirated PDFs circulate, ASME enforces). 17 USC 102(b) excludes procedures/methods/formulas from copyright - only expression is protected, so computing acceptance from formula parameters and citing clause numbers is the legally safer pattern vs embedding code text. ASTM v Public.Resource.Org (DC Cir 2020) held non-commercial posting of standards incorporated-by-reference into law is fair use; government edicts doctrine (Georgia v PRO, 2020) puts law-like content in public domain - but this protects non-commercial public access, NOT a commercial product embedding code text. Safe pattern for compliance software: implement formulas as code, cite clause numbers as facts, let users paste their own licensed excerpts; vendors license ASME collections for internal access rather than redistributing text.
